title.zh: 卷九十五 列傳第二十 高儉五世孫:重 竇威侄:軌 琮 抗 侄孫:靜 誕 侄:璡 從孫:德玄
title.en: Volume 95 Biographies 20: Gao Jian and Fifth Generation Descendents: Gao Zhong, Dou Weizhi, Douzhi, Dou Gui, Dou Cong, Dou Kang, Dou Jing, Dou Dan, Dou Zhi, Dou Congsun: Dou Dexuan
title.raw: 卷九十五 列傳第二十 高儉五世孫:重 竇威侄:軌 琮 抗 侄孫:靜 誕 侄:璡 從孫:德玄 Volume 95 Biographies 20: Gao Jian and Fifth Generation Descendents: Gao Zhong, Dou Weizhi, Douzhi, Dou Gui, Dou Cong, Dou Kang, Dou Jing, Dou Dan, Dou Zhi, Dou Congsun: Dou Dexuan

sentences.zh: 高檢子:履行 審行 真行 五世孫:重 竇威侄:軌 琮 抗 侄孫:靜 誕 侄:璡 從孫:德玄

translations.literal: Sons of Gao Jian: Lüxing, Shenxing, Zhenxing; fifth-generation descendant: Zhong; Dou Wei's nephews: Gui, Cong, Kang; grandnephews: Jing, Dan; nephew: Jin; great-grandson: Dexuan.
translations.idiomatic: The sons of Gao Shilian were Lüxing, Shenxing, and Zhenxing; a fifth-generation descendant was Zhong; Dou Wei's nephews were Gui, Cong, and Kang; his grandnephews were Jing and Dan; his nephew was Jin; and his great-grandson was Dexuan.

sentences.zh: 高儉，字士廉，以字顯，齊清河王岳之孫，父勵樂安王，入隋為洮州刺史。

translations.literal: Gao Jian, courtesy name Shilian, was known by his courtesy name; he was the grandson of Prince Yue of Qinghe of Qi; his father Li was enfeoffed as Prince of Le'an, and after entering Sui served as prefect of Taozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shilian, courtesy name Shilian, was known by that name. He was the grandson of Prince Yue of Qinghe under Northern Qi; his father Li held the title Prince of Le'an and, after the dynasty changed, served the Sui as prefect of Taozhou.

sentences.zh: 士廉敏惠有度量，狀貌若畫，觀書一見輒誦，敏於占對。

translations.literal: Shilian was quick-witted, perceptive, and broad-minded; his appearance was as if painted; what he read once he could recite, and he was sharp in impromptu reply.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian was quick of mind, perceptive, and magnanimous. His features were finely formed, as though painted; he could recite a text after a single reading and was sharp in impromptu debate.

sentences.zh: 隋司隸大夫薛道衡、起居舍人崔祖浚皆宿臣顯重，與為忘年友，繇是有名。

translations.literal: Xue Daohang, chief minister of the Sui Office of the Censorate, and Cui Zujun, attendant of the Secretariat, were both long-serving ministers of high standing; they became friends with him despite the difference in age, and thereby he gained renown.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Daohang of the Office of the Censorate and Cui Zujun, attendant of the Secretariat, were both senior ministers of standing who became his friends across the gap in years. Through them his name spread.

sentences.zh: 自以齊宗室，不欲廣交，屏居終南山下。

translations.literal: Because he was of Qi imperial lineage, he did not wish to cultivate wide acquaintance and lived in seclusion at the foot of Mount Zhongnan.
translations.idiomatic: As a member of the Qi imperial house, he did not wish to cultivate a wide circle of acquaintance and withdrew to live in seclusion at the foot of Mount Zhongnan.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎高孝基勸之仕，仁壽中，舉文才甲科，補治禮郎。

translations.literal: Gao Xiaoji, vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel, urged him to enter office; in the Renshou era he passed the civil-service examination in the top grade for literary talent and was appointed director of rites.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xiaoji, vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel, urged him to take office. In the Renshou reign he passed the civil examination in the top grade for literary talent and was appointed director of rites.

sentences.zh: 斛斯政奔高麗，坐與善，貶為硃鳶主簿，以母老不可居瘴癘地，乃留妻鮮于奉養而行。

translations.literal: When Husizheng fled to Goguryeo, Shilian was convicted of association with him and demoted to chief clerk of Zhuyuan; because his mother was old and could not live in a malarial region, he left his wife Lady Xianyu to care for her and went alone.
translations.idiomatic: When Husizheng fled to Goguryeo, Shilian was punished for association with him and demoted to chief clerk at Zhuyuan. His mother was too old to endure a malarial posting, so he left his wife Lady Xianyu to care for her and set out alone.

sentences.zh: 會世大亂，京師阻絕，交趾太守丘和署司法書佐。

translations.literal: At that time the realm fell into great disorder and the capital was cut off; Qiu He, prefect of Jiaozhi, appointed him judicial secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The realm then fell into chaos and the capital was cut off from the south. Qiu He, prefect of Jiaozhi, appointed him judicial secretary.

sentences.zh: 時欽州俚帥寧長真以兵侵交趾，和懼，欲出迎，士廉曰：「長真兵雖多，縣軍遠客，勢不得久，城中勝兵尚可戰，奈何受制於人？

translations.literal: At the time the Li chieftain Ning Changzhen of Qinzhou invaded Jiaozhi with troops; Qiu He was afraid and wished to go out to submit; Shilian said: "Though Changzhen's troops are many, his army is garrisoned far from home and his men are strangers here—they cannot remain long. The able fighters in the city can still give battle. Why submit to another's will?
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Li chieftain Ning Changzhen of Qinzhou invaded Jiaozhi with his forces. Qiu He was afraid and wanted to go out and surrender. Shilian said, "Changzhen may have many soldiers, but his army is far from home and his men are strangers in this land—they cannot stay long. The city still has troops enough to fight. Why place ourselves at another man's mercy?

sentences.zh: 」和因命為行軍司馬，逆擊破之。

translations.literal: " Qiu He therefore appointed him marching marshal, and he met the enemy and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu He then appointed him marching marshal, and Shilian met the invaders and routed them.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣使徇嶺南，武德五年與和來降，於是秦王領雍州牧，薦士廉為治中，親重之。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor sent envoys to pacify Lingnan, in the fifth year of Wude Shilian came with Qiu He to surrender; the Prince of Qin was then governor of Yong Province and recommended Shilian as chief administrator, treating him with personal regard.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu sent envoys to bring Lingnan under control, Shilian came north with Qiu He to surrender in the fifth year of Wude. The Prince of Qin, then governor of Yong Province, recommended Shilian as chief administrator and held him in high personal esteem.

sentences.zh: 隱太子與王隙已熾，乃與長孫無忌密計計定，是日率吏卒釋囚授甲，趨芳林門助戰。

translations.literal: The rift between the Hidden Crown Prince and the prince had already grown fierce; Shilian therefore joined Long Sun Wuji in a secret plan, and when the plan was settled, that day he led clerks and soldiers, released prisoners and armed them, and hastened to the Fanglin Gate to aid in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: By then the breach between the Hidden Crown Prince and the Prince of Qin had grown bitter. Shilian joined Long Sun Wuji in a secret plan, and when all was settled he led clerks and soldiers that day, freed prisoners and armed them, and rushed to the Fanglin Gate to join the battle.

sentences.zh: 王為皇太子，授右庶子。

translations.literal: When the prince became crown prince, Shilian was appointed right vice tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became crown prince, Shilian was appointed right vice tutor.

sentences.zh: 進侍中，封義興郡公。

translations.literal: He was promoted to attendant-in-ordinary and enfeoffed as Duke of Yixing Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant-in-ordinary and enfeoffed as Duke of Yixing Commandery.

sentences.zh: 坐匿王珪奏不時上，左授安州都督。

translations.literal: He was punished for concealing Wang Gui's memorial and not submitting it promptly, and was demoted to military commissioner of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished for withholding Wang Gui's memorial and failing to submit it in time, and was demoted to military commissioner of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 進益州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to chief administrator of the Great Area Command of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to chief administrator of the Yizhou metropolitan command.

sentences.zh: 蜀人畏鬼而惡疾，雖父母病皆委去，望舍投餌哺之，昆弟不相假財。

translations.literal: The people of Shu feared ghosts and loathed illness; even when parents fell sick they abandoned them; they left their homes and went to inns to take medicine and food; brothers would not even lend one another property.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu feared ghosts and shunned the sick. Even when their own parents fell ill they would abandon them, leave home, and lodge elsewhere to take medicine and food; brothers would not lend one another so much as property.

sentences.zh: 士廉為設條教，辯告督勵，風俗翕然為變。

translations.literal: Shilian established regulations, explained them, and supervised and encouraged the people, and the customs swiftly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian issued regulations, explained them publicly, and supervised and encouraged compliance, and local custom changed almost at once.

sentences.zh: 又引諸生講授經藝，學校復興。

translations.literal: He also invited scholars to lecture on the classics, and schools were revived.
translations.idiomatic: He also invited scholars to lecture on the classics, and the schools were revived.

sentences.zh: 秦時李冰導汶江水灌田，瀕水者頃千金，民相侵冒。

translations.literal: In Qin times Li Bing had diverted the Min River to irrigate fields; land by the water's edge was worth a thousand gold pieces per plot, and the people encroached on one another.
translations.idiomatic: In Qin times Li Bing had diverted the Min River to irrigate the fields. Land along the water fetched a thousand gold pieces per plot, and people encroached on one another's holdings.

sentences.zh: 士廉附故渠廝引旁出，以廣溉道，人以富饒。

translations.literal: Shilian added side channels from the old canal to broaden the irrigation routes, and the people grew rich.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian added side channels branching from the old canal to widen the irrigation network, and the people grew prosperous.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部尚書，進封許國公。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as minister of the Ministry of Personnel and was further enfeoffed as Duke of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as minister of the Ministry of Personnel and was further enfeoffed as Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 雅負裁鑒，又詳氏譜，所署州，人地無不當者。

translations.literal: He was by nature skilled in judgment and selection, and was also well versed in clan genealogies; in every prefecture he assigned men to posts, none was misplaced.
translations.idiomatic: He had a natural gift for judgment and selection and was also deeply versed in clan genealogies; in every prefecture where he assigned men to office, none was misplaced.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩，攝司空，營山陵；

translations.literal: When Gaozu died, Shilian served as acting minister of works and oversaw the imperial tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu died, Shilian served as acting minister of works and oversaw construction of the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 加特進，遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was given the special advance rank and transferred to vice director of the Department of State Affairs, right side.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted special advance rank and transferred to vice director of the Department of State Affairs on the right.

sentences.zh: 士廉三世居此官，世榮其貴。

translations.literal: Shilian's family for three generations had held this office; the age honored their eminence.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian's family had held this office for three generations, and the age counted it a mark of honor.

sentences.zh: 太宗幸洛陽，太子監國，命攝少師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong visited Luoyang, the crown prince supervised the capital, and Shilian was ordered to serve as acting junior preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong went to Luoyang, the crown prince remained in the capital as regent, and Shilian was ordered to serve as acting junior preceptor.

sentences.zh: 手詔曰：「端拱三川，不憂關中者，以屬卿也。

translations.literal: The emperor wrote in his own hand: "I hold court in peace in the Three Rivers region and need not worry over Guanzhong, for I have entrusted it to you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote in his own hand, "I can hold court in peace in the Luoyang region and need not worry over Guanzhong, for I have entrusted it to you.

sentences.zh: 」久之，請致仕，聽解僕射，加開府儀同三司、同中書門下三品，知政事。

translations.literal: " After some time he requested retirement; he was permitted to resign the vice directorship, was given the rank of grand master with the privilege of opening an office equal to the Three Excellencies and the third rank of co-signer at the Secretariat and Chancellery, and continued to participate in governance.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he asked to retire. He was allowed to resign the vice directorship, was given the rank of grand master with privilege to open an office equal to the Three Excellencies and the third rank of co-signer at the Secretariat and Chancellery, and continued to take part in governance.

sentences.zh: 帝伐高麗，皇太子監國駐定州，又攝太傅，同掌機務。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned against Goguryeo, the crown prince supervised the realm from Dingzhou, and Shilian again served as acting grand preceptor and jointly handled affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned against Goguryeo, the crown prince supervised the realm from Dingzhou, and Shilian again served as acting grand preceptor and shared in the handling of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 太子令曰：「寡人資公訓道，而比聽政，據桉對公，情所未安，所司宜別設桉奉太傅。

translations.literal: The crown prince issued an order: "I rely on the Grand Preceptor's instruction in governance, yet when I hear affairs of state and face his desk across from him, my heart is ill at ease; the relevant offices should set up a separate desk for the Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince issued an order: "I rely on the Grand Preceptor's guidance in governance, yet when I hear affairs of state and sit facing him across the desk, I am ill at ease. The relevant offices should set up a separate desk for the Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 」士廉固辭。

translations.literal: " Shilian firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 士廉進止詳華，凡有獻納，搢紳皆屬以目。

translations.literal: Shilian's bearing in advance and retreat was measured and splendid; whenever he offered remonstrance or counsel, the gentry all looked to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian's bearing in court was measured and dignified; whenever he offered remonstrance or counsel, the gentry all looked to him.

sentences.zh: 奏議未嘗不焚稿，家人無見者。

translations.literal: After each memorial or proposal he always burned the draft, and none in his household ever saw it.
translations.idiomatic: After each memorial or proposal he always burned the draft, and no one in his household ever saw it.

sentences.zh: 士廉少識太宗非常人，以所出女歸之，是為文德皇后。

translations.literal: In his youth Shilian recognized that the Prince of Qin was no ordinary man and gave him his daughter in marriage; she became Empress Wende.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Shilian had seen that the Prince of Qin was no ordinary man and gave him his daughter in marriage; she became Empress Wende.

sentences.zh: 及遺令墓不得它藏，惟置衣一襲與平生所好書示先王典訓可用終始者。

translations.literal: In his final instructions he ordered that his tomb hold no other treasures, only one set of clothes and the books he had loved in life that showed the enduring worth of the ancient kings' teachings.
translations.idiomatic: In his final instructions he ordered that his tomb hold no other treasures—only one set of clothes and the books he had loved in life that embodied the enduring worth of the ancient kings' teachings.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗嘗以山東士人尚閥閱，後雖衰，子孫猶負世望，嫁娶必多取貲，故人謂之賣昏。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Taizong had observed that the gentry of Shandong prized pedigree registration; though their houses later declined, their descendants still bore the prestige of former ages, and in marriage they always demanded large bride-prices—hence people called it selling marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Taizong had observed that the gentry of Shandong prized pedigree and lineage; though their houses had declined, their descendants still traded on old prestige, and in marriage they always demanded heavy bride-prices—so people spoke of it as selling marriage.

sentences.zh: 由是詔士廉與韋挺、岑文本、令狐德棻責天下譜諜，參考史傳，檢正真偽，進忠賢，退悖惡，先宗室，後外戚，退新門，進舊望，右膏粱，左寒畯，合二百九十三姓，千六百五十一家，為九等，號曰《氏族志》，而崔幹仍居第一。

translations.literal: Accordingly he ordered Shilian, together with Wei Ting, Cen Wenben, and Linghu Defen, to compile genealogies throughout the realm, consult historical records, verify truth and falsehood, advance the loyal and worthy and remove the perverse and base, putting the imperial clan first and consort kin next, demoting new families and elevating old standing, favoring the well-born and setting aside the humble—altogether two hundred ninety-three surnames and one thousand six hundred fifty-one households in nine grades, titled Records of Clans and Families; yet the Cui clan of Gan still ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly he ordered Shilian, together with Wei Ting, Cen Wenben, and Linghu Defen, to compile genealogies throughout the realm, consult historical records, verify truth and falsehood, advance the loyal and worthy and remove the perverse and base—imperial clan first, consort kin next, new families demoted and old standing elevated, the well-born favored and the humble set aside. They listed two hundred ninety-three surnames and one thousand six hundred fifty-one households in nine grades under the title Records of Clans and Families, yet the Cui clan of Gan still ranked first.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我于崔、盧、李、鄭無嫌，顧其世衰，不復冠冕，猶恃舊地以取貲，不肖子偃然自高，販鬻松檟，不解人間何為貴之？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I bear no grudge against the Cui, Lu, Li, and Zheng clans, but their houses have declined and no longer fill high office; they still rely on old standing to extract bride-prices, and unworthy sons hold themselves proudly aloft, selling off ancestral graves—do they not understand why the world once held them in esteem?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I bear no grudge against the Cui, Lu, Li, and Zheng clans, but their houses have declined and no longer fill high office. They still trade on old standing to extract bride-prices, and unworthy sons hold themselves proudly aloft, selling off ancestral graves—do they not understand why the world once held them in esteem?

sentences.zh: 齊據河北，梁、陳在江南，雖有人物，偏方下國，無可貴者，故以崔、盧、王、謝為重。

translations.literal: Qi held Hebei, and Liang and Chen held the lands south of the Yangtze; though they had men of talent, they were regional states on the margins and had nothing worth esteeming, so the Cui, Lu, Wang, and Xie were held in honor.
translations.idiomatic: Qi held Hebei, and Liang and Chen held the lands south of the Yangtze; though they had men of talent, they were regional states on the margins with nothing truly worth esteeming, so the Cui, Lu, Wang, and Xie were held in honor.

sentences.zh: 今謀士勞臣以忠孝學藝從我定天下者，何容納貨舊門，向聲背實，買昏為榮耶？

translations.literal: Now the strategists and laboring ministers who followed me in settling the realm through loyalty, filial piety, learning, and skill—how can they be ranked below old houses that accept payment, chase reputation over reality, and take pride in buying marriage alliances?
translations.idiomatic: Now the strategists and laboring ministers who followed me in settling the realm through loyalty, filial piety, learning, and skill—how can they be ranked below old houses that accept payment, chase reputation over reality, and take pride in buying marriage alliances?

sentences.zh: 太上有立德，其次有立功，其次有立言，其次有爵為公、卿、大夫，世世不絕，此謂之門戶。

translations.literal: The highest is to establish virtue, next to establish merit, next to establish words, next to hold noble rank as duke, minister, or grandee generation after generation without break—this is what is called a house of standing.
translations.idiomatic: The highest is to establish virtue, next to establish merit, next to establish words, next to hold noble rank as duke, minister, or grandee generation after generation without break—this is what is called a house of standing.

sentences.zh: 今皆反是，豈不惑邪？

translations.literal: Now all is reversed—is this not confusion?
translations.idiomatic: Now all is reversed—is this not confusion?

sentences.zh: 朕以今日冠冕為等級高下。

translations.literal: I shall take those who wear the cap and regalia today as the measure of high and low rank.
translations.idiomatic: I shall take those who wear the cap and regalia today as the measure of high and low rank.

sentences.zh: 」遂以崔幹為第三姓，班其書天下。

translations.literal: " He then ranked the Cui clan of Gan as the third surname and had the book promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He then ranked the Cui clan of Gan as the third surname and had the book promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，許敬宗以不敘武后世，又李義府恥其家無名，更以孔志約、楊仁卿、史玄道、呂才等十二人刊定之，裁廣類例，合二百三十五姓，二千二百八十七家，帝自敘所以然。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Gaozong, Xu Jingzong, because Empress Wu's lineage was not entered, and Li Yifu, ashamed that his own house had no name, again had Kong Zhiyue, Yang Renqing, Shi Xuandao, Lü Cai, and twelve others revise it; they trimmed and broadened the categories, totaling two hundred thirty-five surnames and two thousand two hundred eighty-seven households, and the emperor himself wrote the preface explaining why.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong, Xu Jingzong—because Empress Wu's lineage was not entered—and Li Yifu, ashamed that his own house had no name, again had Kong Zhiyue, Yang Renqing, Shi Xuandao, Lü Cai, and twelve others revise the work. They trimmed and broadened the categories to two hundred thirty-five surnames and two thousand two hundred eighty-seven households, and the emperor himself wrote the preface explaining why.

sentences.zh: 以四後姓、酅公、介公及三公、太子三師、開府儀同三司、尚書僕射為第一姓，文武二品及知政事三品為第二姓，各以品位高下敘之，凡九等，取身及昆弟子孫，余屬不入，改為《姓氏錄》。

translations.literal: The four empresses' surnames, the Duke of Xi, the Duke of Jie, and the Three Excellencies, the crown prince's three preceptors, grand masters with privilege to open an office equal to the Three Excellencies, and vice directors of the Department of State Affairs formed the first surname-grade; civil and military officials of the second rank and third-rank participants in governance formed the second surname-grade; each was ordered by rank high and low in nine grades, taking only oneself and brothers, sons, and grandsons—other relatives were excluded—and the work was retitled Records of Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: The four empresses' surnames, the Duke of Xi, the Duke of Jie, the Three Excellencies, the crown prince's three preceptors, grand masters with privilege to open an office equal to the Three Excellencies, and vice directors of the Department of State Affairs formed the first surname-grade; civil and military officials of the second rank and third-rank participants in governance formed the second; each grade was ordered by rank in nine levels, listing only oneself and brothers, sons, and grandsons while excluding other relatives. The work was retitled Records of Surnames.

sentences.zh: 當時軍功入五品者，皆升譜限，搢紳恥焉，目為「勳格」。

translations.literal: At the time all those who entered the fifth rank through military merit were raised into the genealogical limits; the gentry were ashamed of this and called it the "merit register."
translations.idiomatic: At the time all who entered the fifth rank through military merit were raised into the genealogical limits; the gentry were ashamed of this and called it the "merit register."

sentences.zh: 義府奏悉索《氏族志》燒之。

translations.literal: Li Yifu memorialized that every copy of Records of Clans and Families be seized and burned.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yifu memorialized that every copy of Records of Clans and Families be seized and burned.

sentences.zh: 又詔後魏隴西李寶，太原王瓊，滎陽鄭溫，范陽盧子遷、盧澤、盧輔，清河崔宗伯、崔元孫，前燕博陵崔懿，晉趙郡李楷，凡七姓十家，不得自為昏；

translations.literal: An edict also declared that the seven surnames and ten households—Li Bao of Longxi in Later Wei, Wang Qiong of Taiyuan, Zheng Wen of Xingyang, Lu Ziqian, Lu Ze, and Lu Fu of Fanyang, Cui Zongbo and Cui Yuansun of Qinghe, Cui Yi of Boling in Former Yan, and Li Kai of Zhaojun in Jin—might not marry among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also declared that the seven surnames and ten households—Li Bao of Longxi in Later Wei, Wang Qiong of Taiyuan, Zheng Wen of Xingyang, Lu Ziqian, Lu Ze, and Lu Fu of Fanyang, Cui Zongbo and Cui Yuansun of Qinghe, Cui Yi of Boling in Former Yan, and Li Kai of Zhaojun in Jin—might not marry among themselves.

sentences.zh: 三品以上納幣不得過三百匹，四品五品二百，六品七品百，悉為歸裝，夫氏禁受陪門財。

translations.literal: Officials of the third rank and above might offer no more than three hundred bolts of betrothal gifts; those of the fourth and fifth ranks two hundred; those of the sixth and seventh ranks one hundred—all to serve as the bride's outfit—and the wife's clan was forbidden to accept door-accompanying wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the third rank and above might offer no more than three hundred bolts of betrothal gifts; those of the fourth and fifth ranks two hundred; those of the sixth and seventh ranks one hundred—all to serve as the bride's outfit—and the wife's clan was forbidden to accept door-accompanying wealth.

sentences.zh: 先是，後魏太和中，定四海望族，以寶等為冠。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Taihe era of Later Wei, the eminent clans of the four seas were fixed, with Bao and the others at the head.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Taihe era of Later Wei, the eminent clans of the four seas were fixed, with Bao and the others at the head.

sentences.zh: 其後矜尚門地，故《氏族志》一切降之。

translations.literal: Afterward, because pedigree was prized, Records of Clans and Families demoted them all.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, because pedigree was prized, Records of Clans and Families demoted them all.

sentences.zh: 王妃、主婿皆取當世勳貴名臣家，未嘗尚山東舊族。

translations.literal: Imperial princesses and the consorts of imperial sons-in-law were all taken from the houses of meritorious ministers and famous officials of the age; they never married into the old clans of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princesses and the consorts of imperial sons-in-law were all taken from the houses of meritorious ministers and famous officials of the age; they never married into the old clans of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 後房玄齡、魏徵、李勣復與昏，故望不減，然每姓第其房望，雖一姓中，高下縣隔。

translations.literal: Later Fang Xuanling, Wei Zheng, and Li Ji again intermarried with them, so their prestige did not decline; yet within each surname the branches were ranked by standing, and even within one surname high and low were widely separated.
translations.idiomatic: Later Fang Xuanling, Wei Zheng, and Li Ji again intermarried with them, so their prestige did not decline; yet within each surname the branches were ranked by standing, and even within one surname high and low were widely separated.

sentences.zh: 李義府為子求昏不得，始奏禁焉。

translations.literal: When Li Yifu sought a marriage alliance for his son and could not obtain one, he first memorialized to forbid such marriages.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yifu sought a marriage alliance for his son and could not obtain one, he first memorialized to forbid such marriages.

sentences.zh: 其後天下衰宗落譜，昭穆所不齒者，皆稱「禁昏家」，益自貴，凡男女皆潛相聘娶，天子不能禁，世以為敝雲。

translations.literal: Afterward declining clans fell from the registers; those whom the ancestral line would not acknowledge all called themselves "forbidden-marriage families" and held themselves all the more precious; men and women alike secretly arranged betrothals, and even the Son of Heaven could not forbid it—later ages regarded this as a corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward declining clans fell from the registers; those whom the ancestral line would not acknowledge all called themselves "forbidden-marriage families" and held themselves all the more precious. Men and women alike secretly arranged betrothals, and even the Son of Heaven could not forbid it—later ages regarded this as a corruption.

sentences.zh: 士廉六子，履行、審行、真行有名。

translations.literal: Shilian had six sons; Lüxing, Shenxing, and Zhenxing were renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian had six sons; Lüxing, Shenxing, and Zhenxing were the ones of note.

sentences.zh: 子 履行

translations.literal: Son: Lüxing.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Lüxing.

sentences.zh: 履行居母喪毀甚，太宗諭使強食。

translations.literal: While observing mourning for his mother, Lüxing grieved so severely that Emperor Taizong admonished him and ordered him to force himself to eat.
translations.idiomatic: While observing mourning for his mother, Lüxing grieved so severely that Emperor Taizong admonished him and ordered him to force himself to eat.

sentences.zh: 尚東陽公主，襲爵。

translations.literal: He married Princess Dongyang and inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: He married Princess Dongyang and inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 繇戶部尚書為益州大都督府長史，政有名。

translations.literal: From minister of the Ministry of Revenue he became chief administrator of the Great Area Command of Yizhou, and his governance won renown.
translations.idiomatic: From minister of the Ministry of Revenue he became chief administrator of the Yizhou metropolitan command, and his governance won renown.

sentences.zh: 坐長孫無忌，左授洪州都督，改永州刺史。

translations.literal: He was punished in connection with Long Sun Wuji, demoted to military commissioner of Hongzhou, and then transferred to military commissioner of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished in connection with Long Sun Wuji, demoted to military commissioner of Hongzhou, and then transferred to military commissioner of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 子 真行

translations.literal: Son: Zhenxing.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Zhenxing.

sentences.zh: 真行至左衛將軍。

translations.literal: Zhenxing rose to general of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenxing rose to general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 其子岐連章懷太子事，詔令自誡切，真行以佩刀刺殺之，斷首棄道上，高宗鄙其為，貶睦州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Qi, implicated in the affair of Crown Prince Zhanghuai, was ordered to reprove himself severely; Zhenxing stabbed him with the sword at his belt, cut off his head, and cast it in the road; Emperor Gaozong despised the deed and demoted Zhenxing to prefect of Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qi, implicated in the affair of Crown Prince Zhanghuai, was ordered to reprove himself severely. Zhenxing stabbed him with the sword at his belt, cut off his head, and cast it in the road. Emperor Gaozong despised the deed and demoted Zhenxing to prefect of Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 子 審行

translations.literal: Son: Shenxing.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Shenxing.

sentences.zh: 審行自戶部侍郎貶渝州刺史。

translations.literal: Shenxing was demoted from vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue to prefect of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing was demoted from vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue to prefect of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 五世孫 重

translations.literal: Fifth-generation descendant: Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth-generation descendant: Zhong.

sentences.zh: 士廉五世孫重，字文明，以明經中第，李巽表鹽鐵轉運巡官，善職，凡十年，進累司門郎中。

translations.literal: Zhong, Shilian's fifth-generation descendant, courtesy name Wenming, passed the classics examination, was recommended by Li Xun as patrol officer of the Salt and Iron Transport Office, performed his duties well for ten years in all, and was promoted in succession to director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong, Shilian's fifth-generation descendant, courtesy name Wenming, passed the classics examination. Li Xun recommended him as patrol officer of the Salt and Iron Transport Office; he performed his duties well for ten years in all and was promoted in succession to director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 敬宗慎置侍講學士，重以簡厚惇正，與崔郾偕選，再擢國子祭酒。

translations.literal: When Jingzong carefully selected lecturers for the crown prince, Zhong, for his simplicity, steadiness, and upright honesty, was chosen together with Cui Yan and was twice promoted to director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzong carefully selected lecturers for the crown prince, Zhong—for his simplicity, steadiness, and upright honesty—was chosen together with Cui Yan and was twice promoted to director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 文宗好《左氏春秋》，命分列國各為書，成四十篇。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong favored the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and ordered that the various states be divided, each made into a separate book, completing forty chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong favored the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and ordered that the various states be divided, each made into a separate book, completing forty chapters.

sentences.zh: 與鄭覃刊定《九經》于石。

translations.literal: Together with Zheng Tan he collated and fixed the Nine Classics on stone.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Zheng Tan he collated and fixed the Nine Classics on stone.

sentences.zh: 出為鄂嶽觀察使，以美政被褒。

translations.literal: He went out as observation commissioner of E and Yue and was praised for excellent governance.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as observation commissioner of E and Yue and was praised for excellent governance.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜太子賓客，分司東都。

translations.literal: After some time he was appointed crown prince's guest and served at the Eastern Capital in a nominal post.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed crown prince's guest and served at the Eastern Capital in a nominal post.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted junior guardian of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously granted junior guardian of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：古者受姓受氏以旌有功，是時人皆土著，故名宗望姓，舉郡國自表，而譜系興焉，所以推敘昭穆，使百代不得相亂也。

translations.literal: The commentary says: In antiquity one received surname and clan-name to honor merit; at that time all people were native to the soil, so clans were named by ancestral temple and surname, and each commandery and state set forth its own record—thus genealogies arose, to arrange the ancestral line in order and keep the hundred generations from confusion.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: In antiquity one received surname and clan-name to honor merit. At that time all people were rooted to the soil, so clans were named by ancestral temple and surname, and each commandery and state set forth its own record—thus genealogies arose, to arrange the ancestral line in order and keep the hundred generations from confusion.

sentences.zh: 遭晉播遷，胡醜亂華，百宗蕩析，士去墳墓，子孫猶挾系錄，以示所承，而閥閥顯者，至賣昏求財，汨喪廉恥。

translations.literal: When Jin was driven into exile and barbarian ugliness threw China into chaos, the hundred clans were scattered and broken; though scholars left their ancestral graves, their descendants still carried lineage records to show what they inherited—and among illustrious clans of standing, some went so far as to sell marriage for wealth, drowning integrity and shame.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was driven into exile and barbarian invasions threw China into chaos, the hundred clans were scattered and broken. Though scholars left their ancestral graves, their descendants still carried lineage records to show what they inherited—and among illustrious clans of standing, some went so far as to sell marriage for wealth, drowning integrity and shame.

sentences.zh: 唐初流弊仍甚，天子屢抑不為衰。

translations.literal: In early Tang the abuses still ran deep, yet the Son of Heaven repeatedly suppressed them without success.
translations.idiomatic: In early Tang the abuses still ran deep, yet the Son of Heaven repeatedly tried to suppress them without lasting success.

sentences.zh: 至中葉，風教又薄，譜錄都廢，公靡常產之拘，士亡舊德之傳，言李悉出隴西，言劉悉出彭城，悠悠世詐，訖無考按，冠冕皁隸，混為一區，可太息哉！

translations.literal: By the mid-dynasty, custom and teaching had again grown thin, genealogical records were altogether abandoned, public office no longer bound men to fixed estates, and scholars lost the transmission of old virtue; whoever was surnamed Li was said to come from Longxi, whoever was surnamed Liu from Pengcheng—the generations drifted in falsehood until nothing could be verified; cap and regalia and common clerk were mixed in one mass. Alas!
translations.idiomatic: By the mid-dynasty, custom and teaching had again grown thin and genealogical records were altogether abandoned. Public office no longer bound men to fixed estates, and scholars lost the transmission of old virtue; whoever was surnamed Li was said to come from Longxi, whoever was surnamed Liu from Pengcheng—the generations drifted in falsehood until nothing could be verified, and cap and regalia and common clerk were mixed in one mass. Alas!

sentences.zh: 竇威，字文蔚，岐州平陸人。

translations.literal: Dou Wei, courtesy name Wenwei, was a native of Pinglu in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wei, courtesy name Wenwei, was a native of Pinglu in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 父熾，在周為上柱國，入隋為太傅，太穆皇后，其從兄弟女也。

translations.literal: His father Chi, in Zhou served as pillar of state and after entering Sui became grand preceptor; Empress Taimu was the daughter of his father's younger male cousin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chi, in Zhou served as pillar of state and after entering Sui became grand preceptor; Empress Taimu was the daughter of his father's younger male cousin.

sentences.zh: 威沈邃有器局，貫覽群言，家世貴，子弟皆喜武力，獨威尚文，諸兄詆為書癡。

translations.literal: Wei was deep and far-sighted, with breadth of capacity; he read widely among all books. His family had long been eminent, and the younger men all delighted in martial prowess; Wei alone honored letters, and his elder brothers mocked him as a book-addict.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was deep and far-sighted, with breadth of capacity, and read widely among all books. His family had long been eminent, and the younger men all delighted in martial prowess; Wei alone honored letters, and his elder brothers mocked him as a book-addict.

sentences.zh: 內史令李德林舉秀異，授秘書郎，當遷不肯調者十年，故其學益博。

translations.literal: Li Delin, director of the Secretariat, recommended him as outstanding talent, and he was appointed secretary; when he was due for transfer he refused to accept appointment for ten years, and thereby his learning grew ever broader.
translations.idiomatic: Li Delin, director of the Secretariat, recommended him as outstanding talent, and he was appointed secretary. When he was due for transfer he refused to accept appointment for ten years, and thereby his learning grew ever broader.

sentences.zh: 而諸兄以軍功位通顯矣，薄威職閑冗，更謂曰：「昔仲尼積學成聖，猶棲遲不偶，汝尚何求耶？

translations.literal: His elder brothers by then had risen to prominence through military merit, and finding Wei's post idle and trivial, they again said to him: "Even Confucius, through long study, became a sage, yet he still lingered in misfortune—what more do you seek?
translations.idiomatic: His elder brothers by then had risen to prominence through military merit, and finding Wei's post idle and trivial, they again said to him, "Even Confucius, through long study, became a sage, yet he still lingered in misfortune—what more do you seek?

sentences.zh: 」威笑不答。

translations.literal: " Wei smiled and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Wei smiled and did not reply.

sentences.zh: 蜀王秀辟為記室，威以秀多不法，謝疾去。

translations.literal: Prince Xiu of Shu recruited him as recorder; Wei, because the prince often acted unlawfully, pleaded illness and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiu of Shu recruited him as recorder; Wei, because the prince often acted unlawfully, pleaded illness and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 秀廢，府屬皆得罪，威獨免。

translations.literal: When the prince was deposed, all members of his staff were punished; Wei alone was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was deposed, all members of his staff were punished; Wei alone was spared.

sentences.zh: 大業中，累遷內史舍人，數諫忤旨，轉考功郎中，後坐事免。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he was promoted in succession to attendant of the Secretariat; he remonstrated several times and offended the emperor's will, was transferred to director in the Ministry of Personnel, and later was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye era he was promoted in succession to attendant of the Secretariat; he remonstrated several times and offended the emperor's will, was transferred to director in the Ministry of Personnel, and later was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 後寢疾，帝臨問，及卒，哭之慟。

translations.literal: Later he fell gravely ill; the emperor visited him in person, and when he died the emperor wept bitterly for him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he fell gravely ill; the emperor visited him in person, and when he died the emperor wept bitterly for him.

sentences.zh: 贈同州刺史，追封延安郡公，諡曰靖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted prefect of Tongzhou, further enfeoffed as Duke of Yan'an Commandery, and given the posthumous name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted prefect of Tongzhou, further enfeoffed as Duke of Yan'an Commandery, and given the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 威性儉素，家不樹產，比喪，無餘貲，遺令薄葬。

translations.literal: Wei was by nature frugal and plain; his household accumulated no property, and when he died there was no surplus wealth; his final instructions ordered a simple burial.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was by nature frugal and plain; his household accumulated no property, and when he died there was no surplus wealth. His final instructions ordered a simple burial.

sentences.zh: 詔皇太子、百官臨送。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the crown prince and all officials to attend his funeral.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the crown prince and all officials to attend his funeral.

sentences.zh: 侄 軌

translations.literal: Nephew: Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Gui.

sentences.zh: 兄子軌，字士則。

translations.literal: Wei's brother's son Gui, courtesy name Shize.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's brother's son Gui, courtesy name Shize.

sentences.zh: 父恭，仕周為雍州牧、酂國公。

translations.literal: His father Gong served Zhou as governor of Yong Province and was enfeoffed as Duke of Zan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gong served Zhou as governor of Yong Province and was enfeoffed as Duke of Zan.

sentences.zh: 軌性剛果有威，大業中，為資陽郡東曹掾，去官歸。

translations.literal: Gui was by nature stern, resolute, and commanding; in the Daye era he served as eastern bureau aide of Ziyang Commandery, then left office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was by nature stern, resolute, and commanding. In the Daye era he served as eastern bureau aide of Ziyang Commandery, then left office and returned home.

sentences.zh: 高祖起兵，軌募眾千餘人迎謁長春宮。

translations.literal: When Gaozu raised his army, Gui recruited more than a thousand men and went to meet him at Changchun Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu raised his army, Gui recruited more than a thousand men and went to meet him at Changchun Palace.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賜良馬十匹，使略地渭南，下永豐倉，收兵五千，從平京師。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, bestowed ten fine horses, and sent him to pacify the lands south of the Wei River; he took Yongfeng Granary, gathered five thousand troops, and followed in the pacification of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased, bestowed ten fine horses, and sent him to pacify the lands south of the Wei River. He took Yongfeng Granary, gathered five thousand troops, and followed in the pacification of the capital.

sentences.zh: 封贊皇縣公，為大丞相諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Zanhuang County and appointed advisory aide to the grand chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Zanhuang County and appointed advisory aide to the grand chancellor.

sentences.zh: 稽胡賊五萬掠宜春，詔軌討之。

translations.literal: The Ji-Hu bandits, fifty thousand strong, raided Yichun; an edict ordered Gui to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: When fifty thousand Ji-Hu rebels pillaged Yichun, the emperor ordered Dou Gui to lead a punitive campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 次黃欽山，遇賊乘高叢射，眾為卻。

translations.literal: Halting at Mount Huangqin, they met the bandits shooting down from the heights in dense volleys, and the troops were driven back.
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Huangqin, the rebels rained arrows from the high ground, and Gui's men fell back under the barrage.

sentences.zh: 軌斬部將十四人，更拔其次代之，身擁數百騎殿，令曰：「聞鼓不進者斬。

translations.literal: Gui beheaded fourteen subordinate officers, promoted their next in rank to replace them, personally led several hundred horsemen in the rearguard, and issued the order: "Whoever fails to advance upon hearing the drum shall be beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: Dou Gui executed fourteen of his officers and promoted their deputies to take their places; then, at the head of several hundred horsemen in the rear, he proclaimed: "Any man who hears the drum and does not advance shall die."

sentences.zh: 」既鼓，士爭赴賊，賊射不勝，大破之，斬首千級，獲男女二萬。

translations.literal: When the drum sounded, the soldiers vied to rush the bandits; the bandits' arrows could not hold them off; he inflicted a great defeat, beheading a thousand, and capturing twenty thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: At the beat of the drum, his soldiers surged forward; the rebels' arrows could not stop them. Gui routed the enemy utterly, taking a thousand heads and twenty thousand captives, men and women alike.

sentences.zh: 擢太子詹事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 赤排羌與薛舉叛將鐘俱仇寇漢中，拜秦州總管，討賊連戰有功，餘黨悉降。

translations.literal: The Chipa Qiang and Zhong Juqiu, a rebel general of Xue Ju, raided Hanzhong; he was appointed Prefect-General of Qinzhou; in attacking the bandits he won repeated victories, and the remaining factions all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chipa Qiang joined with Zhong Juqiu, a defector from Xue Ju's ranks, to raid Hanzhong, Gui was appointed Prefect-General of Qinzhou. He fought the rebels in successive engagements with repeated success, until the last of their bands surrendered.

sentences.zh: 復酂國舊封，遷益州道行台左僕射。

translations.literal: His former fief of the State of Zan was restored, and he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Yizhou Circuit Executive.
translations.idiomatic: His old enfeoffment as Duke of the State of Zan was restored, and he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Yizhou Circuit Executive.

sentences.zh: 党項引吐谷渾寇松州，詔軌與扶州刺史蔣善合援之。

translations.literal: The Tangut led the Tuyuhun to raid Songzhou; an edict ordered Gui and Jiang Shanhe, Prefect of Fuzhou, to march to its relief.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut incited the Tuyuhun to attack Songzhou, the court ordered Gui and Jiang Shanhe, prefect of Fuzhou, to go to its aid.

sentences.zh: 善合先期至，敗之鉗川。

translations.literal: Shanhe arrived ahead of schedule and defeated them at Qianchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shanhe arrived first and routed the enemy at Qianchuan.

sentences.zh: 軌進軍臨洮，擊左封，走其眾。

translations.literal: Gui advanced to Lin Tao, struck Zuofeng, and put his forces to flight.
translations.idiomatic: Gui pressed on to Lin Tao, attacked Zuofeng, and drove his followers into flight.

sentences.zh: 度羌必為患，始屯田松州。

translations.literal: Judging that the Qiang would surely become a menace, he began opening military colonies at Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced that the Qiang would remain a lasting threat, he established military farming colonies at Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔率所部兵從秦王討王世充。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to lead his troops with the Prince of Qin in the campaign against Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to take his command and join the Prince of Qin in the campaign against Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 明年，還蜀。

translations.literal: The following year he returned to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he returned to Shu.

sentences.zh: 軌既貴，益嚴酷，然能自勤苦，每出師臨敵，身未嘗解甲，其下有不用命即誅，至小過亦鞭棰流血，人見者皆重足股忄栗，由是蜀盜悉平。

translations.literal: Once Gui had risen high, he grew ever more severe and harsh; yet he could discipline himself to hardship—whenever he took the field he never once doffed his armor; any subordinate who disobeyed was put to death, and even minor faults were punished with the lash until blood flowed; all who witnessed it trembled in dread, and thereby brigandage in Shu was entirely suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: As Gui's rank rose, so did his severity. Yet he drove himself as hard as he drove others: on campaign he never once removed his armor. Any subordinate who failed to obey was executed; even trifling offenses earned the lash until the blood ran. Men who saw it walked as though on thin ice, hearts quaking—and in time every bandit in Shu was brought to heel.

sentences.zh: 初，以其甥為腹心，嘗夜出，呼不時至，斬之。

translations.literal: At first he took his nephew as his trusted confidant; once, when he went out at night and summoned him, the nephew did not arrive promptly, and Gui executed him.
translations.idiomatic: He had once made a nephew his closest confidant. One night he went out and called for the man; when the nephew failed to come at once, Gui had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 又戒家奴毋出外，忽遣奴取漿公廚，既而悔焉，曰：「要當借汝頭以明法。

translations.literal: He had also forbidden his household slaves to go outside; suddenly he sent a slave to fetch gruel from the official kitchen, then regretted it and said, "I must borrow your head to make the law clear."
translations.idiomatic: He had forbidden his household slaves to leave the premises, yet one day he sent a slave to fetch gruel from the official kitchen. Regretting the breach of his own rule, he said, "I must borrow your head to uphold the law."

sentences.zh: 」命斬奴，奴稱冤，監刑者疑不時決，軌並斬之。

translations.literal: He ordered the slave beheaded; the slave cried injustice; the overseer of the execution hesitated to carry it out promptly, and Gui had him beheaded as well.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the slave executed. The slave protested his innocence; the executioner hesitated—and Gui had the executioner beheaded too.

sentences.zh: 後入朝，賜坐禦樓，容不肅，又坐對詔，帝怒曰：「公入蜀，車騎、驃騎從者二十人，公斬誅略盡，我隴種車騎，尚不足給公。

translations.literal: Later he came to court and was granted a seat on the imperial pavilion, but his bearing was not reverent; again he took his seat when receiving an edict, and the emperor in anger said: "When you entered Shu, twenty of my Longzhong cavalry officers accompanied you—you executed nearly all of them; I have barely enough Longzhong cavalry left to supply you."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he came to court and was granted a seat on the imperial gallery, his demeanor was disrespectful; he remained seated even while an edict was being read aloud. The emperor, enraged, said: "When you went into Shu, twenty of my Longzhong cavalry officers went with you—and you killed nearly every one. I can scarcely spare enough Longzhong horsemen to keep you supplied."

sentences.zh: 」因系詔獄。

translations.literal: He was therefore confined in the imperial prison by edict.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial order he was imprisoned in the edict prison.

sentences.zh: 俄釋之，還鎮益州。

translations.literal: Soon he was released and returned to govern Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was released and sent back to his post as military governor of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 軌與行台尚書韋雲起、郭行方素不協，及隱太子誅，詔至，軌內詔懷中，雲起問詔安在，軌不肯示，因執殺之。

translations.literal: Gui and the Executive Directors Wei Yunqi and Guo Xingfang had long been at odds; when the Hidden Crown Prince was executed and the edict arrived, Gui hid it in his bosom; Yunqi asked where the edict was, Gui refused to show it, and had him seized and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Gui had long been at odds with the Executive Directors Wei Yunqi and Guo Xingfang. When the Hidden Crown Prince was put to death and the edict arrived, Gui concealed it in his robe. Yunqi asked where the edict was; Gui refused to produce it and had him seized and killed.

sentences.zh: 行方懼，奔京師，得免。

translations.literal: Xingfang, in fear, fled to the capital and escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Xingfang fled to the capital and so escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 是歲，行台廢，授益州都督，加食邑戶六百。

translations.literal: That year the Executive was abolished; he was appointed Military Governor of Yizhou, with six hundred additional households added to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: That year the circuit executive was abolished. Gui was appointed Military Governor of Yizhou, with six hundred additional households added to his fief.

sentences.zh: 侄 琮

translations.literal: Nephew: Cong
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Dou Cong

sentences.zh: 軌弟琮，有武幹。

translations.literal: Gui's younger brother Cong possessed military talent.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's younger brother Cong was a man of martial ability.

sentences.zh: 大業末，犯法亡命太原，依高祖。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye reign, having violated the law he fled to Taiyuan and attached himself to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye era, after breaking the law he fled to Taiyuan and placed himself in Gaozu's service.

sentences.zh: 與秦王有憾，不自安。

translations.literal: He bore a grudge against the Prince of Qin and did not feel secure.
translations.idiomatic: He had an old grievance against the Prince of Qin and lived in unease.

sentences.zh: 王方收天下豪英，降禮接之，與出入臥內，琮意乃釋。

translations.literal: The Prince was then gathering heroes from across the realm, received them with lowered ceremony and intimacy, and brought Cong in and out of his private quarters; Cong's misgivings were then dispelled.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince was then gathering the finest men in the realm, receiving them with courtesy and warm familiarity, and bringing Cong in and out of his inner chambers. Cong's anxieties gradually eased.

sentences.zh: 大將軍府建，引為統軍。

translations.literal: When the Grand General's headquarters was established, he was appointed a Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand General's headquarters was formed, Cong was appointed a commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 從平西河，破霍邑。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of Xihe and broke Huoyi.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of Xihe and helped break the enemy at Huoyi.

sentences.zh: 授金紫光祿大夫，封扶風郡公。

translations.literal: He was granted the Golden Purple Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Duke of Fufeng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Purple Insignia and enfeoffed as Duke of Fufeng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 從劉文靜擊屈突通於潼關，敗其將桑顯和，通遁去，琮以輕騎追獲于稠桑。

translations.literal: Following Liu Wenjing he attacked Qu Tutong at Tong Pass, defeated his general Sang Xianhe, and when Qu fled, Cong pursued with light cavalry and captured him at Chousang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Wenjing he attacked Qu Tutong at Tong Pass, routed Qu's general Sang Xianhe, and when Qu fled, Cong pursued with light cavalry and captured him at Chousang.

sentences.zh: 進兵下陝縣，拔太原倉。

translations.literal: He advanced and took Shaan County, seizing the Taiyuan granary.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed forward, captured Shaan County, and took the Taiyuan granary.

sentences.zh: 遷左領軍大將軍，賜物五百段。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand General of the Left Leading Army and given five hundred rolls of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand General of the Left Leading Army and rewarded with five hundred bolts of silk and goods.

sentences.zh: 隋河陽都尉獨孤武潛謀歸款，命琮總萬騎，自柏崖迎之，逗留不進，武見殺，坐除名。

translations.literal: Dugu Wu, Sui garrison commander of Heyang, secretly planned to submit; Cong was ordered to lead ten thousand horsemen to meet him from Baiya, but lingered and did not advance; Wu was killed, and Cong was dismissed from office for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Wu, the Sui garrison commander at Heyang, secretly sought to surrender. Cong was ordered to lead ten thousand horsemen to meet him from Baiya, but he delayed and failed to advance. Wu was killed, and Cong was stripped of his rank for the offense.

sentences.zh: 武德初，為右屯衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Early in Wude, he served as Grand General of the Right Garrison Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wude reign he served as Grand General of the Right Garrison Guard.

sentences.zh: 時將圖洛陽，詔琮留守陝，護饟道。

translations.literal: When they were planning an assault on Luoyang, Cong was ordered to remain at Shaan and guard the supply route.
translations.idiomatic: When the court prepared to move against Luoyang, Cong was ordered to hold Shaan and protect the supply lines.

sentences.zh: 王世充將羅士信數以兵鈔絕，琮使人說降之。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong's general Luo Shixin repeatedly cut the route with raiding parties; Cong sent envoys to persuade him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shixin, a general of Wang Shichong, repeatedly raided and severed the supply route; Cong sent envoys to win him over to surrender.

sentences.zh: 東都平，檢校晉州總管。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, he was appointed provisional Prefect-General of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the Eastern Capital fell, he was made acting Prefect-General of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 從隱太子平劉黑闥，以功封譙國公，賜黃金五十斤。

translations.literal: Following the Hidden Crown Prince he pacified Liu Heita; for his merits he was enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Qiao and given fifty catties of gold.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Hidden Crown Prince in the suppression of Liu Heita and, for his service, was enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Qiao and granted fifty catties of gold.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈左衛大將軍，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously awarded Grand General of the Left Guard; posthumous title "Respectful."
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Grand General of the Left Guard, with the posthumous name Respectful.

sentences.zh: 永徽五年，加贈特進。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yonghui he was further posthumously granted the honorary title of Special Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yonghui he received the further posthumous honor of Special Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 侄 抗

translations.literal: Nephew: Kang
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Dou Kang

sentences.zh: 威從兄子抗，字道生。

translations.literal: Wei's elder brother's son Kang, courtesy name Daosheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wei's nephew Kang, whose courtesy name was Daosheng,

sentences.zh: 父榮定，為隋洺州總管、陳國公，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: His father Rongding served as Sui Prefect-General of Mingzhou and Duke of the State of Chen; posthumous title "Virtuous."
translations.idiomatic: His father Rongding had served as Prefect-General of Mingzhou under the Sui and as Duke of the State of Chen; his posthumous name was Virtuous.

sentences.zh: 母，隋文帝姊安成公主也。

translations.literal: His mother was the Princess of Ancheng, elder sister of Emperor Wen of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was the Princess of Ancheng, a sister of Emperor Wen of Sui.

sentences.zh: 抗美容儀，性通率，涉見圖史。

translations.literal: Kang had handsome features and bearing; his nature was frank and straightforward; he had delved into maps and historical works.
translations.idiomatic: Kang was handsome in face and bearing, open and direct in temperament, and well versed in geography and history.

sentences.zh: 以帝甥蚤貴，入太學，釋褐千牛備身、儀同三司。

translations.literal: As the emperor's nephew-by-marriage he rose early to eminence, entered the Imperial Academy, and upon first taking office became a Thousand-Ox Guard Attendant and Director-in-chief of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor's nephew by marriage he rose to prominence early, entered the Imperial Academy, and upon taking his first office became a Thousand-Ox Guard Attendant with the honorary rank of Director-in-chief of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 侍父疾，束帶五旬不弛；

translations.literal: While attending his father's illness he kept his sash tied for fifty days without loosening it;
translations.idiomatic: While nursing his father through illness, he kept his sash tightly bound for fifty days without once loosening it;

sentences.zh: 居喪，哀臒過常。

translations.literal: In mourning, his grief and emaciation exceeded the norm.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning he grieved so deeply that he wasted away beyond what custom required.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，累轉梁州刺史。

translations.literal: He inherited the title and was successively transferred to Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's title and was eventually appointed Governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 將之官，文帝幸其第，酣宴如家人禮。

translations.literal: As he was about to take up office, Emperor Wen visited his residence and they feasted merrily in the manner of family.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to depart for his post, Emperor Wen visited his home and they feasted together with the easy intimacy of kin.

sentences.zh: 母卒，數號絕。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he repeatedly cried until he fainted.
translations.idiomatic: At his mother's death he wept until he repeatedly lost consciousness.

sentences.zh: 詔宮人節哭。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the palace women to restrain their weeping.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict directing the palace women to moderate their lamentation.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，為岐州刺史，轉幽州總管，所至以寬惠聞。

translations.literal: After more than a year he became Governor of Qizhou, then transferred to Prefect-General of Youzhou; wherever he served he was known for leniency and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he was made Governor of Qizhou, then Prefect-General of Youzhou; in every post he was known for his clemency and benevolence.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒反，煬帝疑抗為應，遣李子雄馳往代之。

translations.literal: When Prince Han Liang rebelled, Emperor Yang suspected Kang would respond in sympathy and sent Li Zixiong posthaste to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Han Liang rose in rebellion, Emperor Yang suspected Kang might join him and dispatched Li Zixiong posthaste to relieve him of command.

sentences.zh: 子雄因誣抗得諒書不奏，按鞫無狀，然坐是遂廢。

translations.literal: Zixiong then falsely accused Kang of receiving a letter from Liang and failing to report it; investigation found no substance, yet Kang was dismissed on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zixiong then falsely charged that Kang had received a letter from Liang and concealed it. Though the inquiry found no proof, Kang was dismissed on that pretext.

sentences.zh: 抗與高祖少相狎，及楊玄感反，抗謂高祖曰：「玄感為我先耳，李氏名在圖錄，天所啟也。

translations.literal: Kang and Gaozu had been close since youth; when Yang Xuangan rebelled, Kang said to Gaozu: "Xuangan acts ahead of me; the name Li is recorded in the dynastic registers—Heaven has opened the way."
translations.idiomatic: Kang and Gaozu had been intimate since youth. When Yang Xuangan rebelled, Kang told Gaozu: "Xuangan has merely gone before us. The house of Li is named in the books of destiny—Heaven itself has opened the way."

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「為禍始不祥，公無妄言。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "To speak of disaster at the start is inauspicious—do not speak rashly."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu replied: "To speak of calamity before it comes is ill-omened. Do not talk so recklessly."

sentences.zh: 」煬帝遣抗出靈武，逴護長城，聞高祖已定京師，喜曰：「此吾家婿，豁達有大度，真撥亂主也。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang dispatched Kang to Lingwu to oversee the distant frontier on the Great Wall; when he heard Gaozu had secured the capital, he rejoiced and said: "This son-in-law of my house—open-handed and magnanimous—is a true lord to quell the chaos."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang sent Kang to Lingwu to guard the distant reaches of the Great Wall. When he learned that Gaozu had taken the capital, he rejoiced and said: "That son-in-law of our house—generous and broad-minded—is a true ruler to set the realm right."

sentences.zh: 」因歸長安。

translations.literal: Thereupon he returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 高祖見之喜，握手曰：「李氏果王，何如？

translations.literal: Gaozu received him with joy, clasped his hand and said: "The Li house indeed reigns—what of it?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu welcomed him with delight, clasped his hand, and said: "The house of Li has indeed taken the throne—was I not right?"

sentences.zh: 」因置酒為樂，授將作大匠兼納言，尋罷為左武候大將軍。

translations.literal: He then set out wine for merriment and appointed him Director of Palace Construction and concurrently Palace Counselor; soon after he was removed and made Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He then held a feast in celebration and appointed Kang Director of Palace Construction and concurrently Palace Counselor; soon afterward he was reassigned as Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 帝聽朝，或引升禦坐，既退，入臥內，從容談笑，極平生歡，以兄呼之，宮中稱為舅，或留宿禁省，侍燕豫，然未嘗幹朝廷事。

translations.literal: At imperial audiences the emperor sometimes had him ascend to the imperial seat; after court he would enter the inner quarters and converse and laugh at ease, enjoying the fullest intimacy of a lifetime; he addressed him as elder brother, and within the palace he was called Uncle; at times he stayed overnight in the palace precincts and attended banquets, yet he never meddled in court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During audiences the emperor sometimes summoned him to the imperial dais; after court he would enter the inner apartments and talk and laugh with the ease of old friends, sharing the deepest intimacy of a lifetime. Gaozu addressed him as elder brother, and within the palace he was called Uncle. At times he was kept overnight in the forbidden precincts to attend banquets—yet he never once interfered in affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 後從秦王平薛舉，功第一；

translations.literal: Later he followed the Prince of Qin in pacifying Xue Ju, ranking first in merit;
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed the Prince of Qin in the pacification of Xue Ju and ranked first in merit;

sentences.zh: 又從征王世充。

translations.literal: He also followed the campaign against Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: He also took part in the campaign against Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 東都平，冊勳於廟者九人，抗與從弟軌與焉。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, nine men were enrolled for honors at the ancestral temple, among them Kang and his cousin Gui.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Capital was taken, nine men were enshrined for their achievements in the ancestral temple; Kang and his cousin Gui were among them.

sentences.zh: 賜女樂一部，珍幣不貲。

translations.literal: He was given a troupe of female musicians and treasures beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a company of female musicians and riches beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司徒，諡曰密。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted Minister over the Masses; posthumous title "Diligent."
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Minister over the Masses, with the posthumous name Diligent.

sentences.zh: 子衍、靜、誕，衍襲爵。

translations.literal: His sons Yan, Jing, and Dan—Yan inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Yan, Jing, and Dan; Yan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 侄孫 靜

translations.literal: Grand-nephew: Jing
translations.idiomatic: Grand-nephew: Dou Jing

sentences.zh: 靜字元休，在隋佐親衛，以父得罪煬帝，久不之進。

translations.literal: Jing, courtesy name Yuanxiu, served in the Sui era in the Imperial Guard; because his father had offended Emperor Yang, he long went without promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, whose courtesy name was Yuanxiu, served in the Sui Imperial Guard. Because his father had fallen afoul of Emperor Yang, he languished for years without advancement.

sentences.zh: 高祖入京師，擢并州大總管府長史。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered the capital he was promoted to Chief Administrator of the Taiyuan Grand Prefect-General's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered the capital, Jing was promoted to chief administrator of the Taiyuan Grand Prefect-General's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時突厥數為邊患，糧道不屬，靜表請屯田太原，以省饋運。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks repeatedly troubled the borders and supply lines were cut; Jing memorialized requesting military colonies at Taiyuan to reduce transport costs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Turks repeatedly harassed the frontier and supply lines were unreliable. Jing submitted a memorial proposing military farming colonies at Taiyuan to reduce the cost of transport.

sentences.zh: 議者以流亡未復，不宜重困，於是召入與裴寂、蕭瑀、封倫廷議，寂等不能屈，帝從之，歲收粟十萬斛。

translations.literal: Counselors held that displaced people had not yet returned and should not be burdened further; he was therefore summoned for court deliberation with Pei Ji, Xiao Yu, and Feng Lun; Ji and the others could not refute him, the emperor assented, and the harvest reached one hundred thousand hu of grain annually.
translations.idiomatic: Critics argued that refugees had not yet returned home and ought not be taxed further. Jing was summoned to debate the matter at court with Pei Ji, Xiao Yu, and Feng Lun. None of them could overturn his case; the emperor approved the plan, and the colonies yielded one hundred thousand hu of grain each year.

sentences.zh: 詔檢校并州大總管。

translations.literal: He was appointed provisional Grand Prefect-General of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting Grand Prefect-General of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 又請斷石嶺以為鄣塞，制突厥之入。

translations.literal: He also requested blocking Shiling Pass to serve as a barrier fortress and constrain Turkic incursions.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed closing Shiling Pass and fortifying it as a barrier to check Turkic raids.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，授司農卿，封信都縣男。

translations.literal: When Taizong ascended the throne he was appointed Minister of Agriculture and enfeoffed as Baron of Xindu County.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong came to the throne, Jing was appointed Minister of Agriculture and enfeoffed as Baron of Xindu County.

sentences.zh: 趙元楷為少卿，靜鄙其聚斂，因會官屬大言曰：「如煬帝奢侈，竭四海自奉，司農須公矣。

translations.literal: Zhao Yuankai served as Vice Minister; Jing despised his exactions, and at a gathering of subordinates declared loudly: "Were the emperor extravagant like Yang of Sui, draining the four seas to supply himself, the Ministry of Agriculture would need you."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yuankai served as vice minister, and Jing despised his habit of squeezing revenue. At a meeting of his staff he declared aloud: "If the Son of Heaven were as extravagant as Emperor Yang of Sui, draining the four seas to feed his pleasures, then the Ministry of Agriculture would indeed need you."

sentences.zh: 今天子躬節儉，屈一人安兆庶，惡用公哉？

translations.literal: But today's Son of Heaven personally practices frugality, humbling one man to settle the myriad people—of what use are you?
translations.idiomatic: But today's emperor practices austerity himself, bending one man's pride so that the myriad people may live in peace—what need have we of you?"

sentences.zh: 」元楷大慚。

translations.literal: Yuankai was deeply shamed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankai was utterly humiliated.

sentences.zh: 改夏州都督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Military Governor of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was reassigned as Military Governor of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 突厥攜貳，諸將出征者過靜，靜為陳虜中虛實，諸將由是大克獲。

translations.literal: When the Turks wavered in allegiance, generals setting out on campaign passed through Jing's territory; Jing briefed them on conditions within the barbarian camps, and the generals thereby won great victories in booty.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks grew divided in loyalty, generals setting out on campaign passed through Jing's domain. He briefed them on the true state of affairs among the barbarians, and on that intelligence they won great victories and rich spoils.

sentences.zh: 又間其部落，郁射所部鬱孤尼等九俟斤皆內附。

translations.literal: He also sowed division among their tribes; nine tribal chiefs including Yuguni, under Yüshe's command, all submitted inward.
translations.idiomatic: He also set factions against one another among their tribes, until nine tribal chiefs under Yüshe's command—including Yuguni—all submitted to the court.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，賜馬百匹、羊千口。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this and granted him a hundred horses and a thousand sheep.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his work and rewarded him with a hundred horses and a thousand sheep.

sentences.zh: 及禽頡利，詔處其眾河南。

translations.literal: When Jieli Khan was captured, an edict ordered his people settled south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: After Jieli Khan was taken captive, the court ordered his people resettled south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 靜上書曰：「夷狄窮則搏噬，飽則群聚，不可以刑法繩、仁義教也。

translations.literal: Jing submitted a memorial saying: "When barbarians are destitute they seize and devour; when sated they gather in herds—they cannot be bound by penal law or instructed by benevolence and righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: Jing submitted a memorial: "When the barbarians are desperate they turn to plunder; when they are full they herd together. Neither penal codes nor the teaching of benevolence and righteousness can hold them in check."

sentences.zh: 衣食仰給，不恃耕桑。

translations.literal: They depend on others for food and clothing and do not rely on farming and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: They live on what others provide for food and clothing and do not depend on plowing fields or raising silkworms.

sentences.zh: 今損有為之民，資無知之虜，得之無益於治，失之不害於化。

translations.literal: Now to tax productive subjects to support ignorant barbarians—gaining them does no good for governance, losing them does no harm to civilization.
translations.idiomatic: To burden our productive people in order to sustain these unknowing barbarians is to gain nothing for good government and lose nothing for the civilizing order if they are cast off.

sentences.zh: 況首丘未忘，則一旦變生，犯我王略矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, while the longing for one's native mound is not forgotten, sudden rebellion may arise and violate our royal domain.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, so long as they remember the mounds of their homeland, rebellion may break out at any moment and violate the imperial domain.

sentences.zh: 不如因其破亡，假以賢王一號，妻之宗女，披其土地部落，使權弱勢分，易為羈制，則世為籓臣矣。

translations.literal: Better to exploit their ruin by granting them the title of a worthy king, marrying them to an imperial clan daughter, and dividing their lands and tribes so that authority is weakened and power dispersed, easier to restrain—then for generations they shall be vassal ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Better to take advantage of their present ruin: invest one of them with the title of a worthy king, marry him to a princess of the imperial clan, and break up their lands and tribes so that authority is weakened and power scattered, making them easier to control—then for generations they will serve as vassals of the court.

sentences.zh: 」帝雖不從，然嘉其忠，優詔答曰：「北方之務，悉以相委，以卿為甯朔大使，朕無北顧憂矣。

translations.literal: Though the emperor did not follow his advice, he yet prized his loyalty and replied with a gracious edict: "All northern affairs I shall wholly entrust to you; with you as Grand Ambassador for Pacifying the North, I need have no worry for the northern frontier."
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor did not adopt his plan, he valued Jing's loyalty and answered with a gracious edict: "All affairs of the north I entrust entirely to you. With you as Grand Ambassador for Pacifying the North, I shall have no need to look over my shoulder toward the frontier."

sentences.zh: 」再遷民部尚書。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Minister of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again, to Minister of the Household.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰肅。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title "Solemn."
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Solemn.

sentences.zh: 子逵，尚遂安公主，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Kui married the Princess of Suian and inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kui married the Princess of Suian and inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 侄孫 誕

translations.literal: Grand-nephew: Dan
translations.idiomatic: Grand-nephew: Dou Dan

sentences.zh: 誕，隋末起家朝請郎。

translations.literal: Dan, at the end of Sui, began his career as a Palace Gentleman for Attending Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Dan entered official life at the end of the Sui as a Palace Gentleman for Attending Affairs.

sentences.zh: 義甯初，辟丞相府祭酒，封安豐郡公，尚襄陽公主。

translations.literal: Early in Yining he was recruited as Chancellor's Steward, enfeoffed as Duke of Anfeng Commandery, and married the Princess of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yining era he was appointed Chancellor's Steward, enfeoffed as Duke of Anfeng Commandery, and married the Princess of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 從秦王征薛舉，為元帥府司馬。

translations.literal: He followed the Prince of Qin against Xue Ju and served as Staff Officer of the Marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Prince of Qin in the campaign against Xue Ju and served as staff officer of the marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 累遷太常卿。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 高祖諸子幼，未出宮者十余王，國司家事，皆誕主之。

translations.literal: Gaozu's sons were still young; more than ten princes who had not yet left the palace—all household affairs of their states were managed by Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's sons were still young, and more than ten princes who had not yet left the palace relied on Dan to manage the domestic affairs of their fiefdoms.

sentences.zh: 出為梁州都督。

translations.literal: He went out as Military Governor of Liang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as military governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，召授右領軍大將軍，進莘國公，為宗正卿。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan he was summoned and appointed Grand General of the Right Leading Army, advanced to Duke of the State of Shen, and made Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan reign he was recalled, appointed Grand General of the Right Leading Army, promoted to Duke of Shen, and named Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 太宗與語，昏謬失對。

translations.literal: When Taizong spoke with him, he answered in befuddled confusion.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong questioned him, his replies were muddled and incoherent.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔曰：「誕比衰耗，不能事，朕知而任之，是謂不明。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued: "Dan has lately declined and cannot perform his duties; I knew this yet still entrusted him—this is called being unenlightened."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong then issued an edict: "Dan has grown feeble and can no longer serve effectively. I knew this yet still kept him in office—that is called failing to see clearly."

sentences.zh: 且為官擇人者治，為人擇官者亂。

translations.literal: Moreover, to choose men for offices is governance; to choose offices for men is disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Choosing the right man for the office is good government; choosing the office to suit the man breeds chaos.

sentences.zh: 其以光祿大夫罷就第。

translations.literal: Let him be dismissed as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and retire to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be relieved as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and sent home to his private residence.

sentences.zh: 」卒，贈工部尚書、荊州刺史，諡曰安。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously awarded Minister of Works and Governor of Jing Prefecture; posthumous title "Peaceful."
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Minister of Works and governor of Jingzhou, with the posthumous name Peaceful.

sentences.zh: 侄 璡

translations.literal: Nephew: Jin
