translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Dou Jin

sentences.zh: 抗弟璡，字之推，性沈厚。

translations.literal: Kang's younger brother Jin, courtesy name Zhitui, was by nature deep and steady.
translations.idiomatic: Kang's younger brother Jin, courtesy name Zhitui, was grave and steady by nature.

sentences.zh: 隋大業末，為扶風太守。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye reign of Sui he was Prefect of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui Daye era he served as prefect of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 唐兵起，以郡歸，曆民部尚書。

translations.literal: When Tang forces rose, he submitted the commandery and was successively Minister of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang armies rose, he surrendered his commandery and later served as Minister of the Household.

sentences.zh: 從秦王平薛仁杲，賜錦袍。

translations.literal: He followed the Prince of Qin in pacifying Xue Rengao and was given a brocade robe.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Prince of Qin in the pacification of Xue Rengao and was rewarded with a brocade robe.

sentences.zh: 尋鎮益州，時蜀盜賊多，皆討平之。

translations.literal: Soon he governed Yizhou; at that time bandits and robbers were numerous in Shu, and he attacked and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon assigned to govern Yizhou, where banditry was rife; he suppressed every band in the region.

sentences.zh: 與皇甫無逸不協，數相訴毀，因請入朝，至半道，詔還之。

translations.literal: He was at odds with Huangfu Wuyi and repeatedly accused and slandered each other; he therefore requested to enter court, and halfway there an edict ordered him to return.
translations.idiomatic: He feuded with Huangfu Wuyi, and the two repeatedly denounced each other at court. Jin petitioned to return to the capital, but was ordered back halfway on the road.

sentences.zh: 璡內憂恐。

translations.literal: Jin was inwardly anxious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Jin grew anxious and afraid.

sentences.zh: 會使者至，璡引宴臥內，厚餉遺。

translations.literal: When an envoy arrived, Jin entertained him in his private quarters and gave him a rich parting gift.
translations.idiomatic: When an imperial envoy arrived, Jin entertained him in his inner quarters and sent him away with lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 無逸以聞，坐免官。

translations.literal: Wuyi reported this and Jin was dismissed from office for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi reported the matter, and Jin was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授秘書監，封鄧國公。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Director of the Secretariat and created Duke of Deng.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，遷將作大匠，詔脩洛陽宮，鑿池起山，務極侈浮，費不勝算。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan he was transferred to Director of Palace Construction; an edict ordered him to repair the Luoyang palace, dig pools and raise artificial mountains, striving for utmost extravagance and display, with costs beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he became Director of Palace Construction and was ordered to renovate Luoyang Palace—excavating pools, raising artificial mountains, and pursuing every extravagance until the expense was incalculable.

sentences.zh: 太宗怒，詔毀之，免其官。

translations.literal: Taizong was enraged and ordered it destroyed; Jin was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was furious and ordered the work torn down; Jin was stripped of his post.

sentences.zh: 以酆王納璡女為妃，復位。

translations.literal: Because the Prince of Feng took Jin's daughter as consort, he was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Feng married Jin's daughter, he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈禮部尚書，諡曰安。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously awarded Minister of Rites; posthumous title "Peaceful."
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites, with the posthumous name Peaceful.

sentences.zh: 璡有巧思，工書。

translations.literal: Jin had ingenious ideas and was skilled in calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was ingenious in design and accomplished in calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 武德中，與太常少卿祖孝孫受詔定雅樂，是正鐘律雲。

translations.literal: In Wude, together with Vice Minister of Rites Zu Xiaosun he received an edict to fix the elegant music and correct the bells and pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: During Wude, he and Vice Minister of Rites Zu Xiaosun were commissioned to set the court music and correct the bells and pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 從孫 德玄

translations.literal: Great-grandnephew: Dexuan
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandnephew: Dou Dexuan

sentences.zh: 威從孫德玄，隋大業中，起家國學生。

translations.literal: Wei's great-grandnephew Dexuan, in the Daye era of Sui, began his career as a student of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wei's great-grandnephew Dexuan entered the Imperial Academy at the beginning of his career during the Sui Daye era.

sentences.zh: 祖照，尚周文帝義陽公主，封钜鹿郡公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhao married the Princess of Yiyang, daughter of Emperor Wen of Zhou, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Julu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhao married Emperor Wen of Zhou's daughter, the Princess of Yiyang, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Julu.

sentences.zh: 父彥，襲爵，終隋西平太守。

translations.literal: His father Yan inherited the title and ended his career as Sui governor of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan inherited the title and ended his career as governor of Xiping under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 兄德明，師事陳留王孝逸，通知文史。

translations.literal: His elder brother Deming studied under Wang Xiaoyi of Chenliu and was well versed in literature and history.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Deming studied under Wang Xiaoyi of Chenliu and mastered literature and history.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒反，遣將綦良攻黎州。

translations.literal: When Prince Han Liang rebelled, he dispatched the general Qi Liang to attack Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Han Liang rebelled, he sent the general Qi Liang to attack Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 德明年十八，募士五千，號令嚴整，倍道擊賊，破之。

translations.literal: Deming at eighteen recruited five thousand men; his commands were strict and orderly; marching at double speed he struck the bandits and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Deming, at eighteen, raised five thousand men, drilled them to strict order, forced a rapid march, and routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 以功擢累齊王府屬。

translations.literal: For his merit he was repeatedly promoted as staff of the Prince of Qi's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he rose through successive appointments on the staff of the Prince of Qi's household.

sentences.zh: 坐事免。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was later dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 高祖兵叩長安，而宗室孝基、神符、道宗及竇誕、趙慈景等並系獄，隋將衛文升、陰世師欲殺之，德明諫曰：「罪不在此，殺之無傷於彼，祗取怨焉，不如縱之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu's army knocked at Chang'an, the imperial clansmen Xiaoji, Shenfu, Daozong, and Dou Dan, Zhao Cijing, and others were all imprisoned; the Sui generals Wei Wensheng and Yin Shishi wished to kill them. Deming remonstrated: "The crime does not lie with these men; killing them does no harm to the enemy and only breeds resentment—better to release them."
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu's army reached Chang'an, Xiaoji, Shenfu, Daozong, Dou Dan, Zhao Cijing, and other members of the imperial clan were imprisoned. The Sui generals Wei Wensheng and Yin Shishi planned to execute them. Deming urged: "These men are not guilty of the rebellion. Killing them will not weaken the enemy—only breed hatred. Better to set them free."

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: They therefore stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The execution was halted.

sentences.zh: 長安平，謁高祖，終不自言，時稱長者。

translations.literal: When Chang'an was pacified he went to pay respects to Gaozu and never spoke of it himself; contemporaries called him a man of integrity.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang'an fell he went to see Gaozu but never mentioned his intervention; contemporaries praised him as a man of true integrity.

sentences.zh: 拜考功郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Bureau of Evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of the Bureau of Evaluations.

sentences.zh: 從秦王擊王世充。

translations.literal: He followed the Prince of Qin in attacking Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Prince of Qin in the campaign against Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 封顯武男，曆常、愛二州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Xianwu and successively served as Governor of Chang and Ai prefectures, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He was created Baron of Xianwu, served successively as governor of Changzhou and Aizhou, and died.

sentences.zh: 德玄始為高祖丞相府千牛，曆太宗時不甚顯，高宗以舊臣，自殿中少監為御史大夫，歲中遷司元太常伯。

translations.literal: Dexuan first served as Thousand-Ox Guard in Gaozu's Chancellor's headquarters; through Taizong's reign he was not very prominent; Gaozong, as an old minister, promoted him from Vice Director of the Palace Department to Censor-in-Chief, and within the year to Grand Master of the Bureau of State and Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Dexuan began as a Thousand-Ox Guard on Gaozu's chancellor's staff and remained relatively obscure through Taizong's reign. Gaozong, honoring him as an old servant, promoted him from vice director of the palace department to censor-in-chief and, within a year, to grand master of the bureaus of state and rites.

sentences.zh: 時帝又以源直心為奉常正卿，劉祥道為司刑太常伯，上官儀為西台侍極，郝處俊為太子左中護，凡十餘人，皆帝自擇，以示宰相李勣等，皆頓首謝。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor also personally chose Yuan Zhiyuan as Director of the Bureau of Rites, Liu Xiangdao as Grand Master of the Bureau of Punishments and Rites, Shangguan Yi as Attendant of the Western Terrace, Hao Chujun as Left Protector of the Heir Apparent—in all more than ten men—and showed them to the Chancellor Li Jing and others, who all bowed their heads in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at the same time personally selected Yuan Zhiyuan as director of the Bureau of Rites, Liu Xiangdao as grand master of the bureaus of punishments and rites, Shangguan Yi as attendant of the western terrace, Hao Chujun as left protector of the heir apparent, and more than ten others besides. He presented the list to Chancellor Li Jing and his colleagues, who all bowed in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 麟德初，進檢校左相，勤職約己，天子嘗臨朝，咨其清素，加以賜賚。

translations.literal: Early in Linde he was advanced to provisional Left Chancellor; diligent in office and restrained in personal conduct, whenever the Son of Heaven held court he would inquire after his plain integrity and bestow rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Linde reign he was promoted to acting left chancellor. Diligent and self-restrained, he was questioned at court about his plain living, and the emperor rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 居位數年，贊圖封禪事，與李勣皆為使。

translations.literal: After several years in office he assisted in planning the Feng and Shan rites, and with Li Jing both served as envoys.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in office he helped plan the Feng and Shan sacrifices and, together with Li Jing, served as ritual envoy.

sentences.zh: 帝次濮陽，問古謂帝丘，德玄不能對，許敬宗具道其然，帝稱善。

translations.literal: When the emperor halted at Puyang and asked what antiquity called Diqu, Dexuan could not answer; Xu Jingzong fully explained that it was so, and the emperor praised it.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor paused at Puyang and asked what the ancients had called Diqu, Dexuan could not answer; Xu Jingzong explained the matter fully, and the emperor commended him.

sentences.zh: 敬宗自矜於人，德玄知，不為忤，眾服其量。

translations.literal: Jingzong prided himself before others; Dexuan knew it yet did not take offense, and the multitude admired his magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong was vain before others, but Dexuan knew it and did not quarrel with him; the court admired his forbearance.

sentences.zh: 禮成，進爵二級。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed, his noble rank was advanced by two grades.
translations.idiomatic: After the rites were completed, his noble rank was raised two grades.

sentences.zh: 以弟德遠未及爵，願分封，詔可，故德玄封钜鹿男，德遠樂安男。

translations.literal: Because his younger brother Deyuan had not yet received a title, he requested a divided enfeoffment; the edict approved it, and therefore Dexuan was enfeoffed as Baron of Julu and Deyuan as Baron of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Because his younger brother Deyuan had received no title, Dexuan asked that the enfeoffment be split between them. The emperor agreed: Dexuan became Baron of Julu and Deyuan Baron of Le'an.

sentences.zh: 德玄迎時取合，未嘗有過，然無它補益。

translations.literal: Dexuan accommodated the times and won approval, never committing a fault, yet offered no other substantial benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Dexuan kept pace with the times and pleased his superiors without ever giving offense, yet contributed nothing of lasting substance.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十九，贈光祿大夫，幽州都督，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-nine; posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Military Governor of You Prefecture; posthumous title "Respectful."
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-nine and was posthumously honored as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and military governor of Youzhou, with the posthumous name Respectful.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：高、竇雖緣外戚姻家，然自以才猷結天子，廁跡名臣，垂榮無窮，時有遇合，故見諸事業。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Gao and Dou, though they gained standing through affinal kinship with the imperial house, yet by their own talent and schemes won the Son of Heaven's trust, took their places among famed ministers, and enjoyed glory without end—at times fortune met them, and therefore their achievements appear in the record.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: The Gao and Dou clans rose through imperial marriage, yet it was their own ability that won the throne's trust. They took their places among the great ministers of the age and enjoyed glory that did not fade—when talent met opportunity, their deeds deserved to be recorded.

sentences.zh: 古來賢豪，不遭與運，埋光鏟采，與草木俱腐者，可勝吒哉！

translations.literal: Since antiquity worthy and heroic men who did not encounter their age, whose light was buried and brilliance filed away, rotting together with grass and trees—who can count them? Alas!
translations.idiomatic: How many gifted men of old never found their moment, whose brilliance was buried and left to rot with the grass and trees? It is enough to make one sigh.

sentences.zh: 竇宗自魏訖唐，支胄扶疏數百年，所馮厚矣。

translations.literal: The Dou clan from Wei through Tang, with branches spread for several hundred years, had leaned on great support indeed.
translations.idiomatic: From the Northern Wei through the Tang, the Dou clan's branches spread across centuries on the strength of deep imperial favor.
